context.note:
ELIXIR-DEV implemented REQ-184 strictly per the CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR-approved design (lib/letflow/design/req184-webhook-deliveries-route.md), a tenant-data-path change (new GET route reading webhook_delivery_attempts rows, cross-tenant-404 semantics), hence this hard gate.

WHAT CHANGED:
(1) lib/letflow/webhooks.ex: added Letflow.Webhooks.list_delivery_attempts/3 -- reuses the existing private get/2 helper verbatim for the tenant-scoped subscription existence check (this is what makes cross-tenant-404 automatic, same mechanism update/3 and delete/2 already rely on), then queries Letflow.Webhooks.Delivery filtered by subscription_id, ordered [desc: attempted_at, desc: attempt_count] per the design's OQ-2 disposition, with a database-level Ecto.Query.limit/2. No change to deliver/3, Delivery schema, or any migration.
(2) lib/letflow/routers/webhooks.ex: added a fifth authz_get route clause (GET /subscriptions/:id/deliveries, policy key :WebhookSubscriptionsManage -- already wired in authorization.ex pre-REQ-182, no authorization.ex change made or needed), handle_deliveries/2, resolve_limit/1, and delivery_json/1 (9-field hand-built allowlist matching web/src/types/api.ts's WebhookDeliveryAttempt exactly, confirmed field-by-field). handle_deliveries/2 folds {:error, :not_found} and {:error, :invalid_id} to Response.not_found/1 -- the identical two-clause fold handle_update/2 and handle_delete/2 already use. Moduledoc extended per design section 5.3: route-list sentence now names the fifth route, new '## Delivery attempts (REQ-184)' subsection added, existing '## Contract source' R-Co-not-inspected disclosure left verbatim and its wording covers this route too (moduledoc test asserts this).

DEVIATION FROM THE DESIGN'S OWN TEXT, FLAGGED FOR YOUR ATTENTION: design section 4 says limit is read from conn.params["limit"], claiming Plug's query-string parsing already populates conn.params. That is not true of this router's actual pipeline (Letflow.Api.AuthorizedRouter / use Plug.Router never calls fetch_query_params) -- confirmed by a failing test (conn.params["limit"] was always nil, defaulting every limit test to 20 regardless of the real query param). Fixed by calling fetch_query_params(conn) then reading conn.query_params["limit"] in handle_deliveries/2, matching the established idiom every other query-param reader in lib/letflow/routers/ already uses (dlq.ex, tasks.ex, definitions.ex, tenants.ex, etc. all call fetch_query_params explicitly rather than reading conn.params for a query value). Documented this deviation directly in the router's moduledoc (new paragraph immediately after the Delivery-attempts subsection) rather than silently diverging from the design. This is purely a mechanical fix to reach the design's own intended behavior -- no semantic change to the limit/ordering decisions themselves (OQ-1/OQ-2 unchanged from the design).

ORDERING CHOICE FOR YOUR ATTENTION (design's own OQ-2, carried forward per CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's routing): [desc: attempted_at, desc: attempt_count] -- attempted_at is :utc_datetime (second precision), attempt_count is a populated positive-integer tiebreaker, id (UUIDv4) deliberately excluded as non-chronological. Also OQ-1 (limit default 20, malformed-limit falls back to default rather than 400) is this design's own choice, not stated by any AC.

SECURITY-RELEVANT FACTS TO VERIFY INDEPENDENTLY (not just trust this note):
- INV-2 (response allowlist): delivery_json/1 is a hand-built map literal over %Delivery{} fields -- never Jason.Encoder derivation. tenant_id and the row's own primary key id (distinct from delivery_id) are never emitted.
- INV-5/cross-tenant-404: verified by test (a real subscription in tenant B, with a delivery attempt present, returns 404 to a tenant-A caller with WebhooksManage -- never 403; a malformed id also 404s, never 400). The mechanism is Repo.get(Subscription, id, prefix: prefix) returning nil identically for absent-everywhere and foreign-tenant rows, exactly as update/3/delete/2 already rely on -- no new mechanism introduced.
- INV-8/RT-1 (context-module boundary): grep -n "Repo\.\|Ecto.Query" lib/letflow/routers/webhooks.ex returns zero matches (confirmed, see result.evidence below) -- all Ecto.Query construction lives in lib/letflow/webhooks.ex.
- No change to lib/letflow/api/authorization.ex -- confirmed both required clauses (endpoint_policy_key("GET", "/webhooks/subscriptions/:id/deliveries") and required_permission(:WebhookSubscriptionsManage)) already existed pre-REQ-184 and compile with no duplicate-clause error.
- No change to REQ-183's deliver/3, the Delivery schema, or its migration.

task.description: SECURITY-REVIEWER hard gate (WF-02 Step 2c) on REQ-184's implementation, a tenant-data-path change (new authenticated route reading webhook_delivery_attempts, cross-tenant-404 semantics). Read the approved design (lib/letflow/design/req184-webhook-deliveries-route.md) and the real shipped code (lib/letflow/webhooks.ex's list_delivery_attempts/3, lib/letflow/routers/webhooks.ex's handle_deliveries/2 and delivery_json/1) in full before verdict. Verify against docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md INV-2 (response allowlist -- no tenant_id/internal id leak), INV-5 (cross-tenant-404, not 403 or 400), INV-8/context-module boundary (no Repo/Ecto.Query in the router). Pay particular attention to the resolve_limit/1 fallback (malformed limit silently defaults to 20 rather than erroring, per the design's OQ-1) and confirm this does not itself constitute an injection/DoS surface (it is a plain Integer.parse/1 bound, not string interpolation into a query). PASS/FAIL to Letflow.Api.AuthorizedRouter's REVIEWER next per WF-02 Step 2d.
acceptance_criteria: INV-2: delivery_json/1 emits exactly the 9 contracted fields and no others (no tenant_id, no __meta__, no row primary key id distinct from delivery_id)

INV-5: a caller holding WebhooksManage naming a real subscription id belonging to a different tenant receives 404, never 403, regardless of whether that subscription has delivery attempts; a malformed subscription id also receives 404, never 400
INV-8/RT-1: lib/letflow/routers/webhooks.ex contains zero Repo/Ecto.Query references -- confirm via grep, not just the note above
no unauthorized route or authorization.ex change was introduced beyond what the design specified as already-wired

the fetch_query_params/conn.query_params deviation from the design's literal text is a faithful, non-scope-creeping fix to reach the design's intended limit-parsing behavior, not a silent behavior change

result.summary: Full findings: handoffs/WF02-REQ184-20260830/req184-security-review-findings.md. Diff scope confirmed (git diff main...HEAD --name-only): only lib/letflow/webhooks.ex, lib/letflow/routers/webhooks.ex, test/letflow/webhooks_test.exs, test/letflow/routers/webhooks_test.exs, the design doc, and handoff/status bookkeeping -- no authorization.ex change, no migration. INV-1 APPLIES (tenant-scoped Delivery query) -> PASS, list_delivery_attempts/3 uses Repo.all(query, prefix: prefix); confirmed live via the test run's SQL debug log hitting tenant_<uuid>.webhook_delivery_attempts. INV-2 APPLIES -> PASS, delivery_json/1 hand-built allowlist emits exactly the 9 contracted fields; verified against the full Delivery schema (11 fields total) that tenant_id and the row's own primary key id are both excluded, and no signing/retry-internal/raw-body fields exist on this schema to leak. INV-3 NOT-APPLICABLE (S5 not started). INV-4 APPLIES -> PASS, zero grep hits for hardcoded secrets in the changed files; this diff resolves no secrets. INV-5 APPLIES -> PASS, get/2's Ecto.UUID.cast + Repo.get(Subscription, id, prefix: prefix) makes a foreign-tenant subscription and a nonexistent one both resolve to nil/:not_found identically; both fold to Response.not_found/1, no 400/403 branch; re-ran the real AC4 test (two distinct real provisioned tenant schemas, a real subscription+delivery row in tenant B, probed from tenant A with PLATFORM_ADMIN) and confirmed 404, and confirmed structurally that the subscription-existence check runs and fails before the delivery-attempts query ever executes. INV-6 APPLIES -> PASS (this handoff is the proof artefact). INV-7 APPLIES -> PASS, zero Repo.query hits anywhere in lib/ or priv/repo/migrations/. INV-8 APPLIES -> PASS, one bare {:ok,_}= match found in the router (line 143) but confirmed pre-existing (REQ-182, absent from this diff) via git diff; new code in this diff (handle_deliveries/2, resolve_limit/1, list_delivery_attempts/3) uses case/with throughout, and resolve_limit/1's Integer.parse/1 (never String.to_integer/1) cannot raise on any input including non-numeric, negative, zero, or arbitrarily large values -- also confirmed a large limit poses no resource-exhaustion risk since Ecto.Query.limit/2 bounds it to one subscription's own row set at the database level, not an in-Elixir fetch-then-slice. Independently re-ran (not trusted from ELIXIR-DEV's report): mix compile --warnings-as-errors clean, mix format --check-formatted clean, MIX_ENV=test mix test on both changed test files 39/39 passing, mix letflow.lint_handoffs 0 new violations.
